asset.intro: Each row adds or updates one link.
items: Links missing from the file stay as they are.
The technology must already be in the list: adopt it from the catalog first.
The server matches by its reference (AST-n) when the cell is filled, otherwise by its name.
operating_system: “yes” marks the link as the server's operating system, “no” never marks it.
The export writes these words in the file's language; the import reads them in English, French, German or Spanish.
An empty cell marks a new link of the Operating system family when the server has none yet, as the server page does.
The import never clears a mark.

classification.data_residency_help: The countries where the application stores its data.
classification.business_help: Impact of an interruption on the activity this application supports. Each level states the interruption the activity can tolerate; choose the level whose definition matches.
classification.cyber_help: Choose the highest level justified by a plausible consequence: disclosure, alteration or destruction, interruption, propagation or takeover, physical consequences. Do not confuse cyber criticality with the level of risk!
classification.confidentiality_help: Protection required against disclosure. It informs the cyber assessment without automatically calculating cyber criticality.
classification.recovery_help: Recovery step in the reference recovery plan, chosen according to dependencies. Independent of criticality and without an implicit duration. SaaS may also have a wave; document supplier responsibility.
classification.rto_help: Target recovery time. An RTO at or above the maximum tolerable downtime of the chosen business level is saved with an attention message.
classification.rpo_help: Acceptable data loss expressed as a duration. Zero means no acceptable loss. RPO need not be less than RTO.
classification.name: Name
classification.shown_under_the_name_when_choosing_a_lev: Shown under the name when choosing a level
classification.from_the_most_critical_level_at_the_top_: From the most critical level at the top to the least critical at the bottom.
classification.the_maximum_tolerable_downtime_documents: The maximum tolerable downtime documents each level and warns when an RTO exceeds it.
classification.in_restoration_order_the_first_wave_is_r: In restoration order: the first wave is restored first.
classification.levels_used_to_classify_applications_bus: Levels used to classify applications. Business levels also rate the operational criticality of interfaces and connections.
classification.renaming_reordering_or_retiring_a_level_: Renaming, reordering or retiring a level never changes the applications that use it.
classification.why_these_levels_were_chosen_and_what_th: Why these levels were chosen and what the recovery plan relies on
classification.rto_exceeds_level_downtime: The RTO reaches or exceeds the maximum tolerable downtime (MTD) of the {{level}} level ({{duration}}).
classification.data_at_the_highest_confidentiality_leve: Data at the highest confidentiality level with the lowest cyber criticality: check the cyber assessment.
classification.no_recovery_test_in_the_last_twelve_mont: No recovery test in the last twelve months for an application at the most critical level.
classification.contains_personal_data_help: Check it when the application stores or processes data about identifiable people.
